Skip the on-disk file-hash check when building the VEX document and trust the patch

Pin the VEX document `@id`. See `socket-patch vex --doc-id`
Emit compact (non-pretty) JSON for the VEX document
Path to patch manifest file (resolved relative to --cwd)
Socket API URL (authenticated endpoint). Falls back to the socket-cli config file, then
Socket API token. Absence selects the public patch proxy
Organization slug. Auto-resolved when omitted and a token is set
Public patch proxy URL used when no API token is set [default:
Restrict to these ecosystems (comma-separated): npm, pypi, cargo, gem, golang, maven,
Download installable patched artifacts from the patch service. `service` is the default;
`auto` is a compatibility alias. Local artifact building is no longer supported. Healthy
committed artifacts can be reused offline; missing or corrupt artifacts require a download
Vendored Maven: auto writes the repository tail; none uses only the file repository. The
choice is preserved on subsequent runs
Base URL for the patch vendoring service. Defaults to the active API base (`--api-url`)
when authenticated or the proxy base (`--proxy-url`) otherwise. Override to point `vendor`
at staging / local dev independently of `--api-url`
Override the host of the prebuilt-archive download URL the vendoring service returns. When
set, the CLI rewrites the scheme + host (+ port) of the returned URL to this base,
preserving the path. `vex` and `scan` also accept lockfile URLs on this origin as hosted
patch references (attested, and counted as live hosted wiring) next to patch.socket.dev,
and hosted mode writes a plain http patch URL into a lockfile only for this origin or a
loopback address. Mainly for local-dev / testing, where the host the server bakes into the
URL is not the one to actually fetch from
Disable network access; fail if remote data is needed
Reject modified file content even with --allow-patch-conflicts. Without explicit consent,
mismatches already fail by default. On commands that have --force, --force overrides this
file-content check (but never the separate check for declared project patches)
Accept the risk of conflicts with existing project patches or local modifications when
applying Socket patches. Modified files may be overwritten; patches are not merged
automatically. Backend safety refusals still apply. --yes does not approve patch
Override the path used to discover globally-installed packages
Show extra detail in human-readable output
Preview the operation without making any mutations
Seconds to wait for the `.socket/apply.lock` lock before giving up. By default (or with
`0`) the lock is tried once, failing immediately if another process holds it. A positive
value retries with a 100 ms backoff until the lock frees or the budget elapses. Only
meaningful for the commands that take the lock (`apply`, `rollback`, `repair`, `remove`,
`vendor`, `get` and `scan` when they record, apply, vendor or host patches); other
commands accept it silently. Every holder removes the lock file on exit, so a leftover
from a crashed run never contends
Emit verbose debug logs to stderr
Hosted mode (`scan`/`get --mode hosted`): do NOT auto-configure `trustLockfile: true` in
pnpm-workspace.yaml after a pnpm-lock.yaml (lockfileVersion >= 9) is repointed at the
hosted patch server. pnpm >= 11 rejects the repointed lock without that trust grant, so
opting out means every install needs `pnpm install --trust-lockfile` instead (the run's
warning spells out both recoveries). Only hosted-mode `scan` and `get` read this; other
Hosted mode (`scan`/`get --mode hosted`): do NOT auto-configure `allow-remote=all` in the
project .npmrc after a root package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json is repointed at the
hosted patch server. npm >= 12 defaults to `allow-remote=none` and refuses the repointed
lock (EALLOWREMOTE), so opting out means every install needs `npm ci --allow-remote=all`
instead (the run's warning spells it out). Only hosted-mode `scan` and `get` read this;
Hosted mode (`scan`/`get --mode hosted`, and `rollback`/`remove` of hosted patches): do
NOT remove stale vlt installed copies (`node_modules/.vlt-lock.json` and the stale
`node_modules/.vlt` entries) after `vlt-lock.json` is repointed or restored. vlt never
refreshes an installed copy on its own, so opting out means running `vlt ci` instead (the
run's `redirect_vlt_reinstall_required` advisory says so). Optional dependencies' copies
are never removed. Other subcommands accept it silently
Agent mode (`apply`, `scan`/`get --mode agent`): write a gem patch that changes
native-extension sources WITHOUT rebuilding the extension, for a caller that compiles it
itself. Ruby keeps loading the old build until then, so `vex` and `apply --check` do not
attest those patches (`native_extension_not_rebuilt`). Other subcommands accept it
Hosted mode (`scan`/`get --mode hosted`, and `rollback`/`remove` of hosted patches): do
NOT refresh the gems Bundler already holds for the project (an installed gem under the
project and its cached `.gem`, an archive in `vendor/cache`) after `Gemfile.lock` is
repointed or restored. Bundler keeps an installed gem whatever source the lock names, so
opting out means reinstalling those gems by hand (the run's `redirect_gem_stale_install`
warning names the files). Other subcommands accept it silently
Hosted mode (`scan`/`get --mode hosted`, and `rollback`/`remove` of hosted patches): also
refresh gems in a gem home OUTSIDE the project (the system gems, `~/.gem`, an rbenv or
asdf home). Off by default: another project on the machine may pin the other build of the
same gem version, and its `bundle pristine` would then fail on the replaced archive's
checksum. Other subcommands accept it silently
